title: Solana Surges To $232: ETF Hype And Corporate Adoption Fuel 2025 Crypto Boom | ABC Money
content: Solana (SOL) surged to $232.50 on October 7, 2025, driven by growing institutional interest, corporate adoption, and anticipation around potential spot Solana ETF approvals. Analysts predict SOL could reach $300 by December, with some forecasting a rise to $1,000 by year-end, citing technological advantages and ETF-driven capital inflows. Major asset managers are filing for spot Solana ETFs, with a critical decision deadline on October 10. Institutional confidence is evident through the 20% weekly gain of the REX-Osprey SOL + Staking ETF (SSK), which manages $406.6 million. Pantera Capital’s General Partner Cosimo Jiang forecasts SOL could reach $300–$1,000, while Doo Prime analysts highlight Solana’s scalability edge. Corporate treasuries are increasingly adopting SOL as a reserve asset: HSDT acquired over 2.2 million SOL at ~$235 per token, increasing its combined SOL and cash reserves to over $525 million, making it the second-largest corporate holder after Forward Industries, which holds 6.8 million SOL (valued at over $15 billion). This trend mirrors MicroStrategy’s Bitcoin strategy, emphasizing long-term staking and ecosystem growth. In September and October 2025, firms like DeFi Development Corp, Upexi, and Bit Mining made significant SOL purchases. Solana’s ecosystem reached key milestones: stablecoin supply hit a record $15 billion (nearly triple the January 2025 level), and on-chain metrics soared—TVL reached $12.86 billion and weekly transactions hit 395 million. The MIT-led mumP2P research demonstrated block propagation in under 150 milliseconds on Ethereum’s Hoodi testnet, suggesting Solana could further leverage decentralization for speed, reinforcing its 1,000 TPS advantage over competitors. Solana’s Q3 revenue of $222 million marked four consecutive quarters as the most popular blockchain. Technical indicators support the bullish outlook: the wedge pattern is nearing completion, RSI is at 57 (rising momentum), and MACD shows an upward trend. A breakout above $300 could trigger a cup-and-handle pattern with targets of $500 and $1,000, with long-term projections reaching $8,000. Despite caution due to 20% discounts from all-time highs, sentiment remains strongly positive, with whale accumulation near $229 and elevated altcoin enthusiasm. The convergence of ETF momentum, corporate adoption, technological innovation, and on-chain growth positions Solana as a leading altcoin for 2025.

title: Solana Market Analysis: $2.8B Revenue Milestone Fuels Bullish Case Despite Recent Pullback | Bitcoinist.com
content: Solana (SOL) dipped to $221 at press time, a 3.9% decline over 24 hours, after failing to sustain momentum above $230 and breaking below the 100-hour moving average near $225. Traders are monitoring $218–$212 as immediate support, with deeper bids at $210–$215, while $230–$235 acts as a resistance zone and a heavier supply zone lies between $245–$250. A daily close below $212 risks a drop toward $200, but SOL’s higher-lows on the multi-week chart maintain the broader uptrend. Fundamentally, Solana is showing strong signs of growth: an annualized on-chain revenue of $2.85 billion ($240 million monthly on average) was reported, peaking at $616 million in January during the memecoin surge. Trading platforms contributed 30% ($1.12 billion), with apps like Photon and Axiom generating up to $260 million in a single month. Sub-$0.01 fees and high throughput have enabled Solana’s revenue run-rate to surpass Ethereum’s early-cycle performance, coinciding with 1.2–1.5 million daily active addresses. DeFi metrics reinforce this: $13 billion in total value locked (TVL), 6x year-over-year stablecoin volume growth, and over $500 million in tokenized real-world assets (RWA) indicate durable, non-speculative usage. Upcoming upgrades like Firedancer aim to enhance latency and throughput, strengthening Solana’s competitive moat. Institutional interest is rising, with public balance sheets holding $4 billion in SOL, staking-enabled trust products, and pending U.S. spot SOL ETF applications from Fidelity, VanEck, Grayscale, Franklin Templeton, 21Shares, and Bitwise—many with October 2025 deadlines. Prediction markets suggest a high probability of approval by year-end. Despite near-term volatility from leverage resets, Solana’s revenue scale, user growth, and upgrade pipeline provide a solid foundation. Traders should hold $218–$212 to preserve bullish structure; a breakout above $230 (with volume) could target $245. Long-term investors remain optimistic, with the $300+ price target still viable when risk appetite returns.

title: Solana ETF fee cuts and $6B bet send SOL price into overdrive | Invezz
content: The price of Solana (SOL) rose 4% in 24 hours, reaching approximately $227.71, driven by two major catalysts: aggressive fee cuts in proposed Solana exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and a $6 billion institutional investment commitment. Bitwise announced a revised Solana Staking ETF with a 0.20% annual management fee—waived for the first three months on the first $1 billion in assets—and added staking rewards, positioning it as a low-cost leader in a potential 'fee war' among ETF issuers. This move outpaces competitors like the REX-Osprey Solana Staking ETF, which charges 0.75%. Concurrently, 21Shares expanded its Ethereum ETF to include staking and waived fees for a full year, signaling a broader shift toward active participation in blockchain ecosystems. On the institutional front, Hong Kong-based Helius plans to acquire at least 5% of Solana’s circulating supply—valued at over $6 billion—after securing $500 million for its treasury initiative. The firm, led by former UBS executives Joseph Chee and Zhu Junwei, cites Solana’s technical strength and scalability as key advantages. Technically, SOL reclaimed the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement level at $231.05 after rebounding from $191.63, with the MACD histogram turning positive and the RSI at 54.37, indicating healthy bullish momentum without overbought conditions. A sustained close above $230 could push prices toward $245, though cautious trading volumes persist ahead of the SEC’s ETF decision on October 16, 2025.

title: Solana Real World Assets Hit $500M All-Time High: Will SOL Price Hit $300 in September? - Coinspeaker
